name: ArcticDB
tagline: Serverless DataFrame database from Man Group: Pandas in, versioned columnar data on S3 out.
description: ArcticDB is a C++ storage engine with a Python API that stores Pandas and Polars DataFrames directly on S3, Azure Blob or local LMDB, with no server to run. Every write is versioned, so you can read a symbol as of any earlier version or snapshot, and data is chunked by row and column so slicing by date range and columns stays fast even on very wide tables. It was built by Man Group as the successor to its MongoDB-based Arctic library and open-sourced in 2023 under the Business Source License, with each version converting to Apache-2.0 two years after release. It is a research data store for Python quants, not a SQL database.

license.name: Business Source License 1.1 (converts to Apache-2.0 after 2 years)

pricing.notes: Free under BSL except for offering it as a database service; commercial licences and support are available.

scale.notes: Clients read and write object storage directly, so throughput scales with clients and the store.

strengths: No server: Python clients talk straight to S3, Azure Blob or LMDB
Every write is versioned, with snapshots for reproducible research
Handles very wide DataFrames (hundreds of thousands of columns)
Built and used in production by a large hedge fund
weaknesses: BSL licence restricts offering it as a database service
Concurrent writers to the same symbol need care
Not suited to low-latency streaming or many small writes
useCases: Feature and factor libraries for backtesting
Scientific DataFrame storage on object storage
